summary: Port is bit-for-bit identical to the original at every explicitly-dialed Slope setting; the only divergence is the untouched built-in default (orig 0.4, port 0.5), which tilts the stripes ~5 deg steeper and, on the default 16x16 rig, makes the panel pulse near-solid red/green as the 45-degree stripes align with the grid.
observations: Both sides draw the same thing: scrolling candy-cane diagonal stripes in pure red (255,0,0), pure green (0,255,0) and pure white (255,255,255), no other colors anywhere. Dumped rows on the 48x48 grid at t=0 are character-for-character identical (W GGG W RRR W ... with 1-px white separators between 3-px color runs).

Both are resolution-independent in the same way: a 2D DFT of the R-G field gives a dominant horizontal spatial frequency of exactly 6 cycles per panel width at BOTH 16x16 and 48x48, on both sides. Neither rasterizes at native resolution.

Untouched, the stripe wavevector differs only in its vertical component: original k=(6,5) cycles/panel, port k=(6,6). The port's stripes are therefore exactly 45 degrees; the original's are steeper (~39.8 degrees from horizontal). This holds at t=0 and still holds at t=50-59 s (untouched-late), so it is a constant geometric offset, not a drift.

That offset is exactly one control default. Sweeping sliderSlope on both sides gives ky = 12 x slope on BOTH (slope 0 -> k=(6,0), 0.25 -> (6,3), 0.5 -> (6,6), 0.75 -> (6,9), 1 -> (6,12)). Fractional-frequency scan of the untouched originals puts orig at ky~4.8 (slope 0.4) and port at ky=6 (slope 0.5).

Confirmed directly: rendering the PORT with sliderSlope=0.4 against the UNTOUCHED original on a 48x48 grid gives meanAbsDiff 0.00 at t=0.05, 1 and 2 s, and 0.22 (6 channels of 6912, a single boundary pixel) at t=0. The port's default is the whole difference.

With the SAME slope dialed on both sides, the renders are byte-identical: meanAbsDiff exactly 0.00 at every dumped time at slope 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 and 1 (48x48, 3 dump times each, 6912 channels each).

Baseline (16x16, untouched) statsSummary flags a fake divergence: port zeroMotionFrames 55/120 with motion alternating 0,68,0,68 while orig posts 1/120 and motion ~25-37 every frame. This is NOT a port bug - it is the 45-degree stripe field landing on the same 16-px quantization for pairs of frames. Dialing BOTH sides to slope=0.5 reproduces it on the original exactly (orig zm 55, port zm 55, motion avg 31.2/31.2); dialing both to 0.4 clears it on both (zm 1/1, motion 31.1/31.1).

Same root cause for the port's untouched rhythm image showing periodic bright red/green rows the original lacks (port meanR max 204 vs orig 166 at 16x16): at slope 0.5 on a 16-px panel the stripes periodically align with the columns and the whole panel goes near-solid. dial05-16px reproduces those bright rows on the ORIGINAL, pixel-for-pixel matching the port's untouched rhythm image.

Motion is identical on both sides and fps-invariant. Tracking the phase of the dominant spatial component at 10, 20 and 40 fps gives a per-0.5 s phase advance of -3.409 / -3.404 / -3.409 rad on the original and -3.415 / -3.407 / -3.403 rad on the port - same speed, same direction, no frame-rate coupling on either side.

No modes or regimes. Rhythm images over 60 s at 5 fps and 240 s at 2 fps are homogeneous on both sides from top to bottom; mean brightness holds at 122 with brightnessTrend 'steady' on both, and a --skip 50 window looks like the t=0 window. Single steady scrolling regime, whole run.
Deterministic, no RNG: seed 1234 renders byte-identical to seed 1 (meanAbsDiff 0.00) on both sides.

Control surfaces match exactly: one control on each side, name 'sliderSlope', kind 'slider', label 'Slope'. Neither side binds sensor globals (wantsSensors false on both). No compile or runtime errors on either side.
Probe called sliderSlope responsive on both (orig maxDelta 107.90, port 102.02), and value-dependence is confirmed - 0 and 1 differ from each other and from untouched on both sides.

dials.name: sliderSlope
dials.origEffect: Sets the stripe tilt continuously: vertical spatial frequency = 12 x slope cycles/panel with horizontal fixed at 6, so 0 gives vertical stripes, 0.5 gives exact 45-degree diagonals, 1 gives steep ~63-degree diagonals. Scroll speed and colors unchanged across the sweep. Built-in default (untouched) behaves as 0.4.
dials.portEffect: Identical - byte-identical renders to the original at slope 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 and 1. Only the built-in default differs: untouched the port behaves as 0.5, not 0.4.

feedback: One-line fix, and it is the only fix needed: the port's built-in default for the Slope control is 0.5 where the original's is 0.4. Change the initial value so an untouched load renders a stripe field with 6 horizontal and 4.8 vertical cycles per panel (k=(6,4.8)) instead of 6 and 6. Verified: port at sliderSlope=0.4 matches the untouched original to 0.00 mean absolute difference over a 48x48 grid at t=0.05/1/2 s.

Do not chase the 'port freezes every other frame' signal in the default 16x16 stats (zeroMotionFrames 55/120, motion alternating 0/68) or the periodic near-solid red/green flashes in the port's rhythm image. Both are consequences of the 0.5 default landing the stripes at exactly 45 degrees on a 16-px grid; the original produces the identical artefact when dialed to 0.5, and both disappear once the default is corrected to 0.4.

Nothing else needs touching. Stripe colors (pure 255,0,0 / 0,255,0 / 255,255,255), stripe widths and duty cycle (3-px color runs separated by 1-px white at 48-px width, i.e. 6 cycles/panel), scroll direction and speed (-3.41 rad of spatial phase per 0.5 s, fps-invariant at 10/20/40), control name/kind/label, determinism across seeds, and steady-state behaviour out to 240 s all already match exactly.
